data.headline: Oscar Health Rises As GOP Moderates Rebel Over ACA
data.summary: Oscar Health rallied on Wednesday morning amid an intraparty GOP rebellion over ACA subsidies, though other S&P 500 health care stocks lost more ground.  Centene, the top ACA Marketplace insurer by membership, and HCA Healthcare, the largest U.S. hospital operator, fell for a third straight session, with much of the damage coming Tuesday as House Speaker Mike Johnson signaled he wouldn't allow a vote on a bipartisan compromise plan to extend the subsidies.  On Monday, Morgan Stanley downgraded HCA to underweight from equal weight on Monday, saying its high valuation is at a peak as Washington reins in growth of the ACA Marketplaces and Medicaid supplemental payments.

data.headline: S&P 500 Health Care Stocks Sink With Time Running Out On ACA Subsidies
data.summary: Centene, the top ACA Marketplace insurer by membership, and HCA Healthcare, the largest U.S. hospital operator, are among S&P 500 laggards on Tuesday amid reports that House Speaker Mike Johnson won't allow a vote to renew expiring premium subsidies, but he may not have completely shut the door.  Politico reported that GOP moderates are still working feverishly to come up with a last-minute solution for renewing the ACA subsidies that can win House passage on Wednesday, despite long odds and contentious debates within the Republican caucus.  Humana, the biggest S&P 500 loser on Wednesday, is focused on Medicare Advantage and doesn't offer Affordable Care Act coverage.
